text: The sources provide evidence of tree-cover loss on the property in 2012. The University of Maryland (Hansen/UMD) Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed a tree-cover loss of 1.4 hectares in 2012. The European Commission Joint Research Centre's Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset (GFC2020 V4) corroborates this event, mapping 51% of the event area as forest in 2020. The Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) National forest cartography 2021 indicates that the area was primarily planted forest, with no native forest present. Therefore, the sources agree on the occurrence of tree-cover loss in 2012 on this property.
